findings.what: It teaches the memorised rule "One added inside moves it sideways, the opposite way to the sign", which the brief rules out ("No 'do the opposite' rule for sideways shifts", Zazkis et al., notes 6.6); replace it with the test the rest of the lesson uses: find the input that makes the bracket 0, and the point that sat at 0 now sits there.

findings.where: Screen 7 ("Left 2"), last sentence of the text
findings.what: "A plus inside slides the graph left, the opposite way to its sign" plants the same memorised rule just after the reason; ending on "the bracket is 0 at x = −2, so the bottom sits there" keeps to the brief.

findings.where: Finish panel (FINISH) and the bold last line of explain.text
findings.what: "Changing the input inside, f(x − 3), slides it 3 to the right" is the wording the fact-checker narrowed elsewhere, because f(2x) in lesson 6 also changes the input inside but squeezes the graph; say "taking a number off the input inside".

findings.where: Screen 12 ("A reading 1 mA high"), wrong pick 12.16 mA
findings.what: The red slip dot at (51%, 12.16 mA) is only about 3 px right and 1.5 px above the navy point (2.8 px per percent, 9.3 px per mA) and is drawn underneath it, so the picture barely shows the slip and the red label has to carry it alone.
The rule above the graph reads "S = 0.16p", "S = 0.16p + 1" and so on, then switches to "S(p) = 0.16p + 4" at the end, so the notation changes partway through the slide.

findings.where: Puzzle screens 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 11, 12, and the lead line
findings.what: The three-point table is hidden on every puzzle, even after Check, though the brief says "the table is always on screen" because points convince more than the graph alone, and the lead line promises the table; showing it once the answer is checked would keep both promises.

"A transmitter's reading is 1 mA too high, so it shows S(p) + 1" mixes the transmitter (which sends a current, as screen 3 says) with a reading on a display; "sends 1 mA too much, S(p) + 1" fits an electrician's picture better.
